headline: Meta staff were ranked by AI use. They gamed it.
deck: Big tech companies started ranking staff by how much AI they used, and staff set AI to work on nothing to climb the charts. Why counting AI use backfires, and what to count instead.

headline: Meta staff were ranked by AI use.
They gamed it.

proof.alt: Fortune, 9 April 2026: A Meta employee created a dashboard so coworkers can compete to be the company's No. 1 AI token user

endnote: Checked on 11 November 2026 against the sources below.

figures.after: plus a side business in rats.
figures.alt: How a rat bounty made more rats. Hanoi, 1902: the French paid one cent per rat, with the tail as proof. People snipped the tails and let the rats go, and health inspectors found rat farms outside Hanoi. The city wanted fewer rats; it counted tails.
figures.data_source: Atlas Obscura, The Great Hanoi Rat Massacre of 1902

figures.after: the perfect way to climb a chart that counts usage.
figures.alt: The token leaderboards. A Meta employee's board tracked the tokens used by more than 85,000 Meta staff and ranked the top 250, with titles such as Token Legend and Cache Wizard. Over 30 days usage passed 60 trillion tokens; the top user alone could have cost Meta more than $1.4 million, by Fortune's sums. Meta's board went down two days after the news broke; Amazon's KiroRank, where staff set AI agents on unnecessary tasks, was taken offline over its computing bills.

figures.after: whether the work got any better.
figures.alt: The U-turns. Duolingo, April 2026: its boss said AI use was no longer part of performance reviews. Meta, September 2026: said it would stop using token counts and AI adoption dashboards to judge performance. Amazon, October 2026: told engineers token counts are deeply flawed ways to measure teams' AI use, and that AI not helping is a finding, not a failing.

Half the target, more sales. A medical-device company told about 5,000 staff to send its AI assistant at least 200 queries a month; 31% were repeated or off-task. It cut the target to 100, branch by branch. Total queries fell 30%, nine in ten of the vanished queries junk, and monthly sales among sales staff rose an estimated 7%.
